correctness.rationale: The pointed dual has dimension \(N-1\), and connectedness of the active tight-edge graph exactly enforces rank \(N-1\). With \(1<t<2\), absence of a within-part tight edge forces an integer two-level potential and excludes precisely \(2\sum_i(2^{m_i}-2)\) disconnected oriented binary cuts when \(k\ge3\). If a within-part edge is tight, its unique part has values {0,t} with both attained and every outside vertex has either \(t-1\) or 1, yielding \(\sum_i(2^{m_i}-2)2^{N-m_i}\) connected extremes. The disjoint count is exact. \(t=1\) follows from equilateral geometry and \(t=2\) follows both independently and from the cited 2018 Proposition 3.5. The boundary when every \(m_i=1\) is constant. Twelve independent exact finite enumerations and twenty numerical halfspace computations agree; finite tests are supplementary, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The formula is a full sharp phase diagram for the facet count of real Lipschitz-free balls attached to a natural multidimensional weighted multipartite metric family, with unbounded number of parts and all block sizes. The new two-type tight-graph classification identifies why a continuous metric change creates a combinatorial facet jump, and explains a difference that cannot be read off from either previously published graph endpoint or two-part interpolations. For sizes (2,2,2) the sharp counts are 62,146,56. This is a motivated new complete classification, not an arbitrary isolated computation or an endpoint-table recomputation.
